text:
By mid-March the scaffolding along the eastern wall of Tamsin Reservoir had come down, and the water, long held low for the works, was lapping back toward its old line. The valley has always lent itself to quiet anxiety about dams and what they hold back; the repair, in that sense, was never only an engineering matter.

On 14 March 2024, the project was formally signed off as complete, and the bill was made public. Marguerite Oyelaran-Voss, Director of Capital Works at the Halvern Basin Water Authority, told a public board meeting that the final cost was 48 million.

That figure, set out in the Authority's Tamsin Reservoir Project Closeout Report (Ref. HBWA-CR-2024-07), stands 20% above the original estimate of 40 million. The overrun, the report states, came from reinforcing the eastern spillway wall, work that grew in scope as the repair proceeded.
